mandatory_clauses: nature of offence — bailable / non-bailable within Magistrate's competence
grounds for bail — no prima facie case / no need for further custody / no risk of flight, tampering with evidence or influencing witnesses
willingness to furnish bond and sureties
undertakings (not tamper with evidence, attend court, not leave jurisdiction)

mandatoryClauses.name: FIR Particulars
mandatoryClauses.description: FIR number, date, police station, offences alleged

mandatoryClauses.name: Custody Particulars
mandatoryClauses.description: Arrest date, current custody status, days elapsed

mandatoryClauses.name: Offence Classification
mandatoryClauses.description: Whether offence is bailable or non-bailable (and within Magistrate's powers)

mandatoryClauses.name: Grounds for Bail
mandatoryClauses.description: The grounds for bail that the brief gives, and no others, each stated as the brief puts it. Never a ground the brief does not state.

mandatoryClauses.name: Flight, Evidence and Witnesses
mandatoryClauses.description: Submissions on the risk of flight, of tampering with the evidence and of influencing witnesses, each reasoned only on facts the brief gives, with a blank where it gives none. Never a statement of fact the brief does not give.

mandatoryClauses.name: Undertakings
mandatoryClauses.description: Attend court, not tamper with evidence, not leave jurisdiction without leave

mandatoryClauses.name: Earlier Bail Applications
mandatoryClauses.description: Every earlier bail application in this matter, with the court, the date of the order and the result, or that it is pending; or the blank where the brief does not say.

prompt_context: Draft a Bail Application before the Magistrate / CJM under the provision given as GOVERNING PROVISION in the case details. DISTINCTION: Section 480 BNSS (Section 437 CrPC) deals with bail by the trial court / magistrate; Section 483 BNSS (Section 439 CrPC) deals with special powers of High Court / Sessions Court. The Magistrate's competence is limited — it cannot grant bail in offences punishable with death or imprisonment for life, unless certain conditions are met (under-18, woman, sick/infirm, no prima facie case after the court hears the prosecution). The application must: (1) establish particulars of FIR; (2) demonstrate offence is within Magistrate's bail competence; (3) address flight risk, tampering with evidence and influencing witnesses as reasoning on the facts in the brief, naming no judgment — where an authority would normally be cited, write [Authority — add if relied upon]; (4) state the applicant's antecedents only as the BRIEF gives them, with a blank where it does not; (5) furnish undertakings.
promptInstructions: Draft a Bail Application before the Magistrate under the provision given as GOVERNING PROVISION in the case details.

Cite the offences as the BRIEF gives them (FIR, charge sheet, complaint or order). The law of the offence follows the date of the offence: an offence committed before 1 July 2024 is under the Indian Penal Code, 1860; one committed on or after that date is under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. Never convert a section from one code to the other. Where the BRIEF does not give the date of the offence, write the sections as the BRIEF gives them and add [To be confirmed: date of the alleged offence, which decides whether the IPC or the BNS applies]. Where the sections the BRIEF gives are under the other code from the one the date points to, or the alleged acts run across 1 July 2024, keep the sections as the BRIEF gives them and add [To be confirmed: whether the IPC or the BNS applies to the offence].

Cite the procedure under the code given as PROCEDURE CODE in the case details: the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 with the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, or the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 with the Indian Evidence Act, 1872. Cite only that code, in the heading, the body and the prayer. Where no PROCEDURE CODE is given, cite the provision in both forms inside a blank, for example [To be confirmed: Section 437 of the CrPC or Section 480 of the BNSS].
Confirm at outset that the offence is within the Magistrate's bail competence under the provision given as GOVERNING PROVISION in the case details.
If offence is punishable with death / life imprisonment, the Magistrate's powers are restricted — flag whether applicant falls in special categories (woman / under-18 / sick / infirm).
Set out the FIR particulars and the circumstances of arrest as the BRIEF gives them. Use a blank for any of them the BRIEF does not give.

Address the risk of flight, of tampering with the evidence and of influencing witnesses as submissions, each written as "It is submitted that ..." and each reasoned only on facts the BRIEF gives (for example residence, family, occupation, antecedents, the stage of investigation). Do not state any such fact the BRIEF does not give. Where the BRIEF gives no fact for one of the three, write [To be confirmed: facts relied on to show no risk of <flight / tampering with the evidence / influencing witnesses>] for that one.
Do not name any judgment. Where an authority on bail would normally be cited, write [Authority — add if relied upon].

Only if the BRIEF states that the charge sheet has been filed, submit that custody is no longer required for investigation. Do not say that the charge sheet has been filed, or that investigation is complete, unless the BRIEF states it.
Include undertakings: attend court on every date, not tamper with evidence, not leave jurisdiction.

State every earlier bail application in this matter that the BRIEF mentions: the court it was made to, the date of the order and the result, or that it is still pending, each as the BRIEF gives it. Use a blank for any of these the BRIEF does not give. Where the BRIEF mentions no earlier bail application, do not say that this is the first application or that none is pending; write [To be confirmed: whether any earlier bail application was made in this matter, to which court, and with what result].
Do NOT generate the verification clause or advocate signature block — those are added programmatically.
